title: Alcohol Fuels a Dangerous Divide — TikTok
notes: Story follows the article's arc: alcohol's toll → where you're born matters → Nevada vs Utah → the laws on each side → Wisconsin → who dies → fewer people drinking → what works.
All figures are from the article (Sep 3, 2025) and the sources it cites (CDC, BRFSS, Gallup, NHTSA).

post.headline: Why drinking deaths fall by half from Nevada to Utah
post.caption: Alcohol kills more Americans than opioids and suicides combined, and where you're born changes the odds. Crossing from Nevada to Utah cuts the excessive drinking rate in half, from 24% to 12%. Utah's 0.05 blood alcohol limit cut its fatal crash rate by almost 20% in a year.
post.cta: Full story and interactive maps at the link in bio.

headline.text: Alcohol kills more Americans than {opioids and suicides combined.}

say: Alcohol kills more Americans than opioids and suicides combined.
Every three minutes, one person in America dies because of alcohol.
Depending on where you are born, you may be far more likely to die from alcohol.

scenes.source: Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System · American Inequality
say: Stepping across the state border from Nevada to Utah cuts the excessive drinking rate in half.

scenes.title: Adults who drink excessively
say: In Lincoln County, Nevada, 24% of adults drink excessively, compared with 12% in Washington County, Utah.
Nevada has the weakest liquor laws in the nation, with liquor sold 24/7 and no last call.
Utah has some of the strongest, with metered pours and no liquor sales on Sundays.

stats.label: higher in Nevada than in Utah

say: The death rate from alcohol in Nevada is twice as high as it is in Utah.

overlays.label: drinking deaths per 100,000, up from 6.7 in 1999

say: Drinking deaths in Wisconsin nearly tripled between 1999 and 2020.

scenes.title: How much more likely to die from alcohol
scenes.source: Alcohol Fuels a Dangerous Divide · American Inequality
say: Native Americans are five times more likely to die from alcohol than White Americans, and low-income Americans twice as likely as the wealthy.

overlays.label: more liquor stores where poverty tops 20%

scenes.source: Alcohol Fuels a Dangerous Divide · American Inequality
say: Liquor stores concentrate in poor neighborhoods, with 50% more of them where poverty tops 20%.
Only 54% of American adults now say they drink, the lowest share in ninety years.

stats.label: fatal crash rate in its first year

say: Utah is the only state with a 0.05 blood alcohol limit, and its fatal crash rate fell almost 20% in the first year.
Cities like Baltimore have capped liquor licenses in poor neighborhoods, which can prevent hundreds of homicides a year.
You can read the full story on American Inequality.
